topic: Digit-placement dependency synthesis under simultaneous divisibility and minimization

cognitive.X: Determine the order in which the given digit-multiset, divisibility rules and minimality constrain positions.
cognitive.Y: Previously established divisibility by9, alternating sums for11, and last-two-digit divisibility by4.
cognitive.Z: Link the automatic digit-sum check, alternating position partition, final-two-digit constraint and lexicographic minimization without violating a previous dependency.
cognitive.W: Independently decide to use the alternating-position partition before final-two-digit selection and place the earliest legal prefix, then revise that ordering under an added mod7 demand.
cognitive.wrong_idea: Satisfy each divisibility condition independently then concatenate valid endings, or assume the smallest initial digits always yield a valid final number.
cognitive.replacement_rule: Use the fixed digit sum, split positions to satisfy mod11, impose a compatible suffix divisible by4, then prove minimality by excluding all lexicographically smaller prefixes.

difficulty_proposal.basis: Interlocking position assignment, one automatic condition, and changed mod7 constraint defeat a single fixed construction; D4 proposed for route novelty and exception-sensitive minimization.
difficulty_proposal.adjacent_D3_alternative: If the constraints are provided in execution order, or a learner only fills a prepared table, it is likely D3. Reviewer must confirm independently selected dependency order and transfer warrant.

core2a.prompt: Use each of the six distinct digits 0,1,2,3,4,8 exactly once to make the smallest positive six-digit integer divisible by 9, 11 and 4. A six-digit number may not begin with zero. Establish that your result is minimal without simply citing a computer search.
givens: All three divisibility requirements must hold simultaneously.
core2a.H1: Which divisibility test becomes automatic from a fixed digit multiset?
core2a.H2: How does the test for11 constrain the two groups of alternating positions while the last-two-digit rule constrains the ending? Do not choose the winning prefix.
core2a.H3_after_nonblank: The six digits sum18, so mod9 is automatic. For mod11 the two alternating position sums must both be9; compare candidate prefixes lexicographically before fixing a mod4 suffix.
core2a.math_proof: Any arrangement has digit sum18. Its alternating digit sum is 2S_odd−18, an even integer from −18 to18; divisibility by11 forces it to be0, hence odd-position and even-position sums both9. Leading prefix10 fails because positions3 and5 would need to sum8 from {2,3,4,8}, impossible. Prefix12 with digit0 in position3 forces digit8 in position5, and remaining 3 and4 must occupy positions4 and6; ending84 works but 83 does not. Thus 120384 is minimal.

core2b.changed_task: Keep all three original divisibility conditions and digits, but additionally require divisibility by7. Find and justify the new smallest number.
core2b.changed_reason: The only qualifying prefix12 candidates are 120384 and 128304; neither is divisible by7. The next possible prefix13 has valid 130284, divisible by4,7,9,11.
core2b.different_W: Reopen minimization after adding an independent global factor; cannot simply keep the prior minimum.

role_plans.CORE1: Orient digit multiset, fixed sum and independent positional constraints; show generic formulas only.
role_plans.CORE1A: Use a different four-digit digit set {0,1,2,6} to construct an independently checked example divisible by9 and4; learner exits on a new small changed-number constraint.
role_plans.CORE1B: Repair the wrong idea of independently picking a small prefix and legal final two digits; use a separate four-digit impossible leading-zero/position case for a falsifying boundary.
role_plans.CORE2A: Six-digit simultaneous constraints requiring learner to select dependency order and prove smallest number without a prefilled winning partition.
role_plans.CORE2B: Add divisibility by7; same digit multiset and previous rules but a changed new optimum.

independent_oracle.method: Exhaust all permutations of [0,1,2,3,4,8] with nonzero leading digit and verify mod4,mod9,mod11, then add mod7; assert min, count and analytical prefix exclusions.
